mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses when inflation expectations rise sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered quarters, or GDP growth recovers within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE by at least 0.4 percentage points over three months signals a tightening labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation does not accelerate.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in INDPRO of more than 1% indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate output and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered events, or the decline in INDPRO reverses within one month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in CPIAUCSL over the same month signals a restrictive monetary policy with declining inflation, which can lead to a short-term risk-off environment and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases AND CPIAUCSL decreases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or CPIAUCSL resumes rising within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST over two months signals deteriorating housing and overall demand, which reduces consumer spending and capital expenditures, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or either series rebounds within one month.

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS rises while UNRATE is flat or falling over three months, it indicates increased labor participation without wage growth, which can temporarily boost corporate profits but ultimately signals labor cost pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE does not rise over three months
regime_hint: labor supply expansion without wage inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or wage growth accelerates within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between rising RSAFS and positive S&P 500 5-day returns, as increased household savings can signal confidence and future consumption, supporting near-term equity gains.
failure_condition: The correlation between RSAFS increases and positive 5-day S&P 500 returns falls below statistical significance (p > 0.10) in a rolling 3-year window.
